chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, by his chain, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one whose fingers move faster than his tongue, so (he will be) counted in his favour.

key_terms.أَصَابِعُهُ: his fingers (referring to physical movements in prayer)
key_terms.حُسِبَ لَهُ: counted in his favour / recorded as merit

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for being quick to perform prayer?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* is often interpreted to mean that the physical readiness and haste of the limbs are rewarded as a sign of sincere devotion, provided the recitation follows correctly. It underscores the importance of *khushu'* (focus) and the spiritual value of eager participation in worship, linking physical action with inner intent. This concept is frequently discussed in the context of the etiquette of prayer, emphasizing that the body's promptness reflects the heart's eagerness to meet God.
